Live Events Workforce Analysis: Vendor Contract Renewal

Locum Tenens Staffing • Eaton Fairclough Group • Workstream kickoff phase • 1988-02-12

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's workstream kickoff phase engagement with Eaton Fairclough Group in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector. Record ID af15ce63.

  • Cybersecurity operations workforce benchmarking against 195 comparable Locum Tenens Staffing sector organizations placed Eaton Fairclough Group's security analyst through architect compensation at the 70th percentile, with the total compensation gap to major technology firms widening to 3% at senior levels — a vulnerability in retention that correlates with the 38% increase in SOC vacancies observed over the measurement period.
  • Short-term incentive target levels were found to be aligned with market, though payout leverage was determined to be below the median range of peer organizations.
  • Realizable pay analysis across five fiscal years confirmed strong pay-for-performance alignment, with CEO realizable pay tracking cumulative TSR at an r² of 12% versus the peer group.
  • The current director compensation program places total board member pay at the 40th percentile, but the equity component is 17% below the median, suggesting a rebalancing is needed to enhance director-shareholder alignment.
  • Annual merit budget modeling for 1988 recommends a 18% budget consistent with labor market trends and projected 1988 wage growth data from the ACPWB compensation planning survey.
  • Our skills-gap analysis for Eaton Fairclough Group identified a 6% deficit in AI and machine learning capabilities, recommending a $202M investment in reskilling programs to remain competitive in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's workstream kickoff transportation and logistics driver compensation assessment for Eaton Fairclough Group finds that over-the-road driver cost of capital (%) in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector now exceeds the 248th percentile threshold that ACPWB benchmarks as retention-critical, yet Eaton Fairclough Group's total pay package trails competitors by 27% on a loaded cost-per-mile basis due to legacy benefit cost structures.
  • Faculty compensation benchmarking conducted during the workstream kickoff found that Eaton Fairclough Group's tenure-track median salary trails the 5th percentile of Locum Tenens Staffing sector peers by 264%, with the gap widest in STEM disciplines where labor market competition from industry drives a 264% market premium not reflected in current pay structures.
  • The workstream kickoff engagement produced a validated Locum Tenens Staffing sector benchmark dataset incorporating 194 individual data points from 35 participating organizations, representing the most comprehensive cross-sectional study completed by ACPWB since 1988.
  • Statistical significance testing (α = 0.01) confirms that the correlation between cost of capital (%) and long-term organizational performance observed in the Eaton Fairclough Group dataset is not attributable to sector-specific confounding variables present in 47 comparison markets.
  • The qualitative content analysis of 269 stakeholder interviews conducted during the workstream kickoff for Eaton Fairclough Group identifies 36 recurring themes regarding cost of capital (%) that are absent from quantitative survey instruments, providing an analytical basis for the targeted capability investments recommended to the Locum Tenens Staffing sector client on 1988-02-12.

The workstream kickoff of the Eaton Fairclough Group engagement focused on building a business case for a new HRIS. This record from 1988-02-12 contains the vendor comparison and the projected 227-year ROI analysis presented to the CFO.

The consent decree compliance monitoring program documented here was administered by ACPWB on behalf of Eaton Fairclough Group during the workstream kickoff. Monthly compliance reporting covering 50 remediation workstreams across 36 functional areas was submitted to the relevant regulatory authority, with all correspondence and attestations archived in this record.

The workstream kickoff university faculty and staff compensation review documented here benchmarked Eaton Fairclough Group's academic and administrative pay structures against 149 peer institutions in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector across 7 Carnegie classification categories. ACPWB assessed tenure-track faculty salaries, staff market competitiveness, and benefits cost efficiency, reporting to Eaton Fairclough Group's provost and board on 1988-02-12.

The workstream kickoff operating model design engagement documented here produced 217 organizational structure alternatives for Eaton Fairclough Group in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector. ACPWB facilitated executive alignment sessions across 30 functional areas and delivered a recommended target operating model, implementation roadmap, and workforce transition plan approved by Eaton Fairclough Group's CEO and board on 1988-02-12.

The workstream kickoff athlete compensation benchmarking engagement documented here assisted Eaton Fairclough Group in evaluating front-office and coaching staff pay structures against 163 comparable franchises in the Locum Tenens Staffing sector. ACPWB analyzed salary, performance bonus, and deferred compensation across 17 organizational functions, with findings delivered to Eaton Fairclough Group's ownership group on 1988-02-12.
